transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. Before we get started, could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Um, yeah—so I came in because I feel like I just cannot keep everything organized, especially with schoolwork and my little accessories shop I’ve been trying to run. It’s like, I’ll have assignment notes in one pile, receipts in another pile, supplies kind of everywhere, and then due dates written down somewhere but not where I can actually find them when I need them.

And I keep trying to set it all up in a way that makes sense, but then it turns into these stacks of papers and beads and packaging stuff and notebooks, and I’ll sit down to do one thing and realize I don’t even know what I’m supposed to do first. Like, is this the assignment that’s due sooner, or should I be packing an order, or finding the receipt I need, or organizing the supplies before I can even start? It just gets really overwhelming, and I feel like I’m constantly behind even when I’ve technically been “working on things,” if that makes sense.
Thinking back, did you have similar struggles with staying organized, focused, or finishing tasks when you were a child, say before age 12?

Yeah, I think so. I mean, I don’t remember every detail from being that little, obviously, but my mom has actually kept some of the notes from elementary school, like teacher comments and stuff, and they kind of say the same thing over and over.

It wasn’t so much that I didn’t understand the work—like I could do it—but the notes would say I was always getting out of my seat, or talking before I was called on, or kind of blurting things out. And with group activities, I guess I would rush ahead or push to get things done really fast, even when I knew what we were supposed to be doing. My mom has shown me those notes before, and it’s honestly a little embarrassing because it sounds very much like me, just smaller.
In the past six months, do you often find yourself feeling restless, fidgety, or having trouble staying seated during work, meetings, or classes?

Yeah, definitely. It’s kind of hard to explain, but even if I’m technically just sitting there, my body doesn’t feel settled. It feels like there’s this buzzing under my skin, like I need to move or shift or do something, even when I’m not actually going anywhere.

It’s especially noticeable when I’m supposed to sit still and listen, like in class or if someone is explaining something for a while. I’ll be sitting there trying to look normal, but inside I’m like, okay, I need to move my legs, or change position, or mess with something in my hands. It’s not always that I’m trying to leave or anything—it’s more like my body just won’t be quiet.

Would you say these organizational and restlessness difficulties are causing real problems in more than one area of your life—like both at school and in running your shop, or with friends and family too?

Yeah… it’s definitely not just one area. I wish it was, because then I could kind of tell myself it’s just school being stressful or just the shop being chaotic, but it’s both.

With school, it’s actually gotten kind of serious. I missed some required steps for my program—like things I was supposed to complete or submit or follow up on—and now my financial aid is at risk. Which is really scary, because it’s not like I didn’t care. I just kept thinking I’d get to it, or I’d have the paper somewhere, or I’d remember what the next step was, and then suddenly it was past the point where it was just a small mistake.

And with the shop stuff, people I’ve worked with on projects have started depending on me less. Like, they’ll kind of take over things I was supposed to handle, or they won’t ask me first anymore, and I can tell it’s because they’re not sure I’ll actually follow through in the way they need. That feels awful, because I really do want to be reliable. I’m not trying to make extra work for anyone. But from their side, I get why they’d be frustrated. It’s been affecting how much people trust me with things.
Do you currently use alcohol, recreational drugs, or stimulant medications not prescribed to you?

Um… I’m not totally sure how to answer that in the way you mean. Like, do you mean any use at all, even occasional, or more like whether I’m using something regularly or to help me focus?

I don’t want to give you the wrong answer by guessing what counts. Could you clarify what you mean by “currently use”?
To clarify, I mean any use at all, even occasional—do you currently drink alcohol, use any recreational drugs, or take stimulant medication that wasn't prescribed to you, even just once in a while?

I’m honestly not totally sure how to answer that because I don’t really have a clear thing to report there. Like, nothing comes to mind that I’m using in that way or that I’ve been tracking as a “current use” thing.

I don’t take stimulant medication that isn’t mine or anything like that. And as far as alcohol or recreational drugs… I don’t think there’s anything regular or significant to mention. If you mean absolutely any tiny occasional thing, I’d have to think about it, but there isn’t something I’m relying on or using to get through school or focus or calm down.

Have you ever had a distinct period—lasting several days—where you felt unusually elevated, euphoric, or irritable, needed much less sleep than usual but still had lots of energy, or felt you could do anything?

I don’t think so… at least nothing that clearly fits that. I mean, I’ve had times where I’m really worked up or I get excited about something and I’ll talk a lot or jump into a bunch of plans, but I don’t know that it’s ever been like a distinct several-day period where I felt euphoric or like I could do anything.

The sleep part is kind of what makes me pause, because if I sleep badly I’m usually tired, not magically energized. I don’t really remember having days where I needed way less sleep and still had tons of energy in that unusual way. And irritability, I mean, I can get irritated, but I wouldn’t say it comes in some separate episode like that. So… no, not that I’ve noticed.
Do you often forget important things like appointments, obligations, or where you put everyday items, even when you're trying hard to remember?

I’m not sure how to answer that clearly. I mean, I do misplace things sometimes, like normal stuff, but I don’t know if I’d say it’s “often” or that it’s with important things specifically. I’d have to really think through examples, because nothing huge is jumping out at me right this second.

With appointments or obligations, I don’t think there’s a major pattern I’ve noticed, but I also kind of rely on reminders and checking things, so it’s hard to separate whether I’m naturally remembering or whether the reminders are doing the work. But I don’t want to say yes if I’m just thinking of ordinary forgetfulness.

So… I guess my answer is maybe sometimes, but I’m not sure it’s a big or consistent problem.

In the past six months, do you often find yourself interrupting or finishing other people's sentences, blurting out answers before a question is fully asked, or having trouble waiting your turn in conversations or lines?

Yeah… I think that one does happen. Mostly in class discussions or group critiques, like when someone is explaining their point or asking something, I’ll jump in before they’re actually finished. It’s not even always because I’m trying to be rude or dominate the conversation—I kind of think I know where they’re going, and then my answer just comes out.

And then sometimes I realize halfway through that I guessed wrong, or that they weren’t done, and I feel really embarrassed. Like I’ll be sitting there thinking, “Why did I do that? I could’ve waited two more seconds.” It happens enough that I notice it, especially in group settings where everyone is supposed to take turns talking.
